name: AD825 (single high-speed JFET-input op amp)
tagline: A cheap, fast single JFET op amp (41 MHz, 125 V/us, 12 nV/rtHz). DIY op-amp rollers call it punchy and rich, and LC Audio sold it as an upgrade part.
technology: A single JFET-input, high-speed, voltage-feedback op amp from Analog Devices. ADI's SPICE macro-model (JCH / ADI Central Apps, 1999) uses a P-channel JFET differential input pair. The datasheet specifies it fully at +/-5 V and +/-15 V. The orderables found are SOIC-8 and a 16-lead wide SOIC (R-16); the R-16 was added in datasheet Rev. F (10/04). No dual or quad version exists.

reputation.summary: A niche cult part from the mid-2000s op-amp-rolling era. Head-Fi users call it punchy and intimate, with a rich timbre and thick texture that suits female vocals and strings; one fan of 2x AD825 on an adapter says 'AD825 is the best'. Others hear it as flat or unemotional in some DACs, or as more coloured and a bit closed-in than the AD797. The LME49990 was reported as smoother, with a firmer low end. LC Audio Technology sold AD825 upgrade parts. Audio Asylum and diyAudio threads reportedly suggest it as a better replacement for the AD712 in the Parasound HCA-2200 MK-I input stage. No objective audio measurements were found. All sonic claims are forum opinion.
sonic_descriptors: good for female voices and strings
flat / unemotional in some DACs (dissenting view)
coloured and a bit closed-in compared with the AD797 (dissenting view)
less smooth, lighter low end than the LME49990 (comparison)
typical_uses: Op-amp rolling in DAC and CD-player analog stages, on SOIC-to-DIP adapters (two AD825s per dual socket)
Drop-in upgrade for AD711/AD712-class JFET op amps (forum discussion, e.g. Parasound HCA-2200 MK-I)
caveats: Single-channel and surface-mount only (SOIC-8 / SOIC-16). Replacing a DIP dual needs an adapter carrying two chips.
It is a 41 MHz part, so adapter wiring and local decoupling matter (general high-speed practice; no AD825-specific oscillation reports were found).
It needs more supply headroom to swing 2 V into 330 ohm than parts such as the AD823 (8.6 V vs 6.1 V minimum in the Tangentsoft test).
The praise is subjective forum opinion. No published THD+N measurements were found. The forum sources were not re-checked in this pass.

silicon_changes.when: 4 Aug 2010 (PCN 10_0117 publication date per search summary); form at Rev. A
part_numbers_affected: AD825AR-16 / AD825ARZ-16 (16-lead SOIC_W; inferred from the PCN's SOIC_W scope)
AD825AR / AD825ARZ (named by an earlier search summary; doubtful, since these are 8-lead SOIC_N)
silicon_changes.identification: Only the SOIC_W package (the -16 suffix) is in scope. Distinguish by date code after the PCN effective date and by the Carsem M assembly site.
silicon_changes.summary: PCN 10_0117, 'Halogen Free Material Change for SOIC_W Products at Carsem', moves SOIC_W assembly from Carsem S (Ablestik 84-1LMISR4 or 8290 die attach; Sumitomo 6600H or G700 mold compound) to Carsem M (Henkel QMI-519 die attach; Hitachi CEL8240F10 mold compound). It was part of ADI's move to halogen-free 'green' packages and was qualified per AEC-Q100. The AD825 has a 16-lead SOIC_W option (AD825ARZ-16), which is the version plausibly affected. The die does not change.

spec_deltas.before: Carsem S; Ablestik 84-1LMISR4 or 8290 die attach; Sumitomo 6600H or G700 mold
spec_deltas.after: Carsem M; Henkel QMI-519 die attach; Hitachi CEL8240F10 mold (halogen-free)

silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - package materials and assembly site only; same die, pinout and data sheet
silicon_changes.verification: Three searches showed that PCN 10_0117 is a halogen-free die-attach and mold-compound change for SOIC_W at Carsem, not a die change. They also confirmed that the AD825 has a 16-lead SOIC_W variant (AD825ARZ-16). The earlier listing of the 8-lead AD825AR/ARZ conflicts with the SOIC_W scope and is flagged as doubtful.

counterfeit_notes: No AD825-specific counterfeit reports were found. The known orderables are SOIC-8 (AD825AR/ARZ) and SOIC-16 wide (AD825ARZ-16). No DIP-8 or dual version was found, though the ordering guides of Rev. A and Rev. C were not read. A bare DIP-8 chip marked 'AD825', as opposed to a SOIC chip on a DIP adapter, should be treated as suspect (inference). Buy from ADI-authorised distributors (DigiKey 505-AD825ARZ-ND, Mouser, Farnell), and check the ADI logo, the date and lot code, and consistent laser marking.

revision_chain_notes: Analog Devices AD825 datasheet (sole vendor; no second sources found). Chain, oldest to newest: Rev. 0 (presumed, mid-1990s, no copy found); Rev. A (date unknown, pre-2/01; Carnegie Observatories copy); Rev. B (presumed, no copy found); Rev. C (date unknown, pre-2/01; 100y.com.tw copy); Rev. D (2/01; no copy URL found); Rev. E (between 2/01 and 10/04; no copy found); Rev. F (10/04; R-16 SOIC added; no copy URL found); Rev. G (4/14; current; copies at analog.com, RadioLocman, U of Toronto, device.report, and now dcddcc.com). This pass added one more Rev. G mirror (dcddcc.com) and several third-party copies whose revision is not shown: AllDatasheet 48430 (AD825ACHIPS), EHAM.RU AD825AR, DatasheetQ/DatasheetBank ID 264067, datasheetspdf/datasheet4u ID 142611. Two of these are candidates for pre-Rev. F editions: EHAM AD825AR and AllDatasheet 48430 (the low ID and 'General Purpose' wording without a hyphen). Only direct inspection can confirm them. Two ADI product-page URLs were added as Wayback seeds. Still missing: any copy of Rev. 0, Rev. B, Rev. D, Rev. E and Rev. F; the original release date (Rev. 0); the dates of Rev. A, B, C and E; the change logs for Rev. A through D and for F to G. The current datasheet's package list reads 'RW-16', while the earlier history says 'R-16' for the 16-lead SOIC; this needs checking in Rev. F/G.
